clue.text: The last tight game you mentioned broke his record and his heart, maybe

definitions.text: broke his record and his heart, maybe

indicators.note: tight is slang for drunk, and a drunk word staggers its letters out of order
something mentioned is spoken, so the sound of the word counts rather than its spelling

blocks.note: Z is the last letter of the alphabet
the four letters of game rearranged
the letter U is pronounced like you

explanation.surface: A sports commentator says the final close match shattered a player's record and broke his heart.
explanation.walkthrough: U sits inside the shuffled game, after its first letter, and Z leads. The definition is itself an example of the device: 'broke' governs both a record and a heart in different senses.
explanation.definitionFit: A zeugma is a figure of speech where one verb governs two objects in different senses, as broke does with record and heart.

clue.text: They made Spurs supporter finally smile … or panic!

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the word it follows
in a panic things are thrown into disorder, so the letters are scrambled

blocks.note: last letter of supporter
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Tottenham fan torn between grinning and panicking.
explanation.walkthrough: Spurs is the nickname of Tottenham Hotspur, a London football club, so the capital S hides the riding spurs that lorimers made.
explanation.definitionFit: Lorimers were craftsmen who made bits, stirrups and spurs and other metal parts of horse harness.

clue.text: Apprentice loses head but he brings home the bacon

indicators.note: losing its head means the word drops its first letter

blocks.note: an apprentice is a learner

explanation.surface: A trainee is demoted yet remains the family's breadwinner.
explanation.definitionFit: To bring home the bacon is an idiom for earning the household's income, which is what an earner does.

clue.text: Want massage reported

indicators.note: reported means passed on by word of mouth, so the sound matters

blocks.note: to knead is to massage, as a masseur works muscles

explanation.surface: Someone saying they would like a rubdown.
explanation.definitionFit: Want and need are synonyms, both meaning to require or lack something.

clue.text: Worker and speaker taking exercise

indicators.note: taking in something means holding it inside, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: an orator is a public speaker
PE is physical education, school exercise

explanation.surface: An employee and a public speaker go off to do some exercise together.
explanation.walkthrough: PE goes after the first letter of the speaker.
explanation.definitionFit: An operator is someone who works a machine, a general term for a worker.

clue.text: Way one stops little (Scottie) dog

indicators.note: to stop something is to plug it, so these pieces sit inside the other word

blocks.note: wee is Scottish for little
ST is short for street, a way
Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A street-crossing scene where one small Scottish terrier blocks the way.
explanation.walkthrough: ST and I go between the second and third letters of the Scottish word for little.
explanation.definitionFit: A Westie is a West Highland white terrier, a small Scottish breed, hence the bracketed Scottie.

clue.text: Gutted — one sector struggling? This should stop the rot

indicators.note: a gutted word has lost its insides, leaving just its outer letters
struggling suggests writhing and twisting, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: first and last letters of one
taken as written

explanation.surface: A disappointed manager whose struggling business sector needs something to halt its decline.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gutted' reads as a dash-separated cry of disappointment, but it trims the word one.
explanation.definitionFit: Creosote is a tar-based wood preservative painted on fences to prevent decay, literally stopping rot.

clue.text: Cross — judge defending old queen exempt from tax

indicators.note: defending means guarding by surrounding, so the other letters enclose this piece

blocks.note: a zo is a cross between a yak and a cow
Elizabeth Regina, the late Queen
to rate is to judge or assess

explanation.surface: An angry judge protects an elderly queen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross' looks like an adjective for angry; it is a crossbred animal, the zo (also dzo or zho), a Himalayan yak-cattle hybrid.
explanation.definitionFit: To zero-rate goods is to apply a VAT rate of nothing, so they are effectively exempt from the tax.

clue.text: Pornographer firstly has a rule about body part

indicators.note: firstly picks out the opening letter of the word before it
about suggests turned around and moved about, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: first letter of pornographer
the letters of a rule rearranged

explanation.surface: A smut-peddler insists on a rule concerning the human body.
explanation.definitionFit: The pleura is the membrane lining the chest cavity and enveloping the lungs, an anatomical part.

clue.text: Harry arguing endlessly — language!

indicators.note: endlessly means the word loses its final letter
to harry is to harass and trouble, so the letters are pushed around

blocks.note: arguing without its last letter

explanation.surface: Someone called Harry keeps arguing and swearing; mind your language!
explanation.walkthrough: 'Harry' reads as a name; it is a verb meaning harass.
explanation.definitionFit: Ugrian is a branch of the Finno-Ugric family, including Hungarian, so it names a language group.

clue.text: Dutch helping for as long as it takes

blocks.note: Du. is the dictionary abbreviation for Dutch
a ration is a portion or helping

explanation.surface: Going Dutch on a meal, where everyone takes a helping for as long as it lasts.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase 'for the duration' means for as long as it takes, so the definition is that phrase with the answer standing in.
explanation.definitionFit: A duration is the whole length of time something lasts, which is how long it takes.

clue.text: Cheese brought over in three napkins

indicators.note: in says the letters lie inside the words that follow
brought over means turned back the other way, so read right to left

blocks.note: letters running across the two words

explanation.surface: A waiter brings cheese to the table wrapped in three napkins.
explanation.definitionFit: Paneer is a fresh, unsalted cheese used in South Asian cooking.

clue.text: Warehouse in French town rejected drinker

indicators.note: something rejected is sent back, so the word runs backwards

blocks.note: en is French for in
T is the map abbreviation for town
a toper is a heavy drinker

explanation.surface: A drunk is turned away from a storehouse in a French town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'French town' wants to be read together; 'in French' and 'town' are separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: An entrepot is a trading port or depot where goods are stored before re-export, a kind of warehouse.

clue.text: Slowly destroy what a Norseman did, said East Ender

indicators.note: this is how a Cockney Londoner would pronounce it, dropping the initial aitch, so sound matters

blocks.note: Vikings rowed their longships, so he rowed

explanation.surface: A Cockney describing how a Viking slowly wrecked something.
explanation.walkthrough: An East Ender is a Londoner from the East End, whose Cockney accent drops the H of he.
explanation.definitionFit: To erode is to wear away gradually, as water wears down rock.

clue.text: Food served to us lacks taste to begin with — shameful!

indicators.note: to lack something is to be without it, so a letter is removed
to begin with points to the opening letter of the word before it

blocks.note: a dish on our table is food served to us
first letter of taste, the one removed

explanation.surface: A diner complains that the meal is so bland it is a disgrace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Food served to us' expands to a whole phrase, dish on our table; dropping its T leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Dishonourable means bringing disgrace or lacking honour, a synonym of shameful.

clue.text: Slander retracted at start — surprise (bigly) for Trump

indicators.note: retracted means drawn back, so the word runs in the opposite direction

blocks.note: mud-slinging is slander
to found something is to start it

explanation.surface: A politician's slander is withdrawn as soon as it begins, to Trump's huge surprise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Surprise (bigly)' means surprise greatly; 'bigly' is a word associated with Donald Trump, and the spelling without B is a recognised variant.
explanation.definitionFit: To dumfound, or dumbfound, is to astonish someone so greatly that they are struck speechless.

clue.text: I'm done with pub — virtually ruined smoking area

indicators.note: virtually means almost, so the word is cut short of its final letter
ruined letters have been wrecked and must be rebuilt in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
pub missing its last letter

explanation.surface: A smoker gives up on a pub almost wrecked by the smoking ban.
explanation.definitionFit: An opium den is a place where people gathered to smoke opium, literally an area for smoking.

clue.text: Bush's ideal running mate originally

indicators.note: running suggests the letters are on the move and land in a new order
originally means at the start, telling us where the word placed before it goes

blocks.note: bud is American slang for a mate or friend
the letters of ideal rearranged

explanation.surface: George Bush's perfect choice of running mate in a presidential election.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bush' wants to be the US president and 'running mate' a political phrase; the bush is the shrub, and running and mate split apart.
explanation.definitionFit: Buddleia is a flowering shrub, often called the butterfly bush.

clue.text: Radiant young woman on the internet I have to follow

blocks.note: E as in email, electronic
a miss is a girl or young woman
I've, apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: A glowing young influencer online whom I need to follow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Follow' sounds like social-media following, but it just places I've last.
explanation.definitionFit: Emissive means giving out radiation or light, so something emissive is radiant.

clue.text: Spit, slightly twisting plant

indicators.note: a slight twist moves only a little, so just two letters swap places

blocks.note: saliva is spit

explanation.surface: Someone spits while turning slightly.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the I and V change places.
explanation.definitionFit: Salvia is the sage genus, a plant grown for herbs and flowers.

clue.text: Two countries flipped over the same newspaper feature

indicators.note: over here means placed around, so the pair encloses the other piece
flipped means turned the other way, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: US and UK
do is short for ditto, the same

explanation.surface: Two nations flip over the same story in the papers.
explanation.walkthrough: Each country is flipped separately and they sit either side of DO.
explanation.definitionFit: Sudoku is the number puzzle printed in newspapers alongside the crossword.

clue.text: Riot — elite forces finally getting on top

indicators.note: finally picks out the closing letter of the word before it
in a down answer, on top means placed first above the rest

blocks.note: last letter of forces
the cream is the elite, the best

explanation.surface: Special forces finally take control of a riot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Elite forces' reads as one unit; the two words split.
explanation.definitionFit: A riot and a scream are both informal words for someone or something hilariously funny.

clue.text: Got rid of king, conspiracy theorist ultimately admitted

indicators.note: ultimately means at the very end, so the final letter of the word is taken

blocks.note: K is king in chess notation
David Icke, a well-known British conspiracy theorist
last letter of admitted

explanation.surface: A monarch is deposed, and a conspiracy theorist eventually owns up to it.
explanation.walkthrough: David Icke is a former British TV sports presenter now known for conspiracy theories about reptilian rulers.
explanation.definitionFit: To kick a habit is to give it up, so kicked means got rid of.

clue.text: Peer at rich bloke's lover

blocks.note: a nob is a wealthy, upper-class person
leman is an old word for a lover or sweetheart

explanation.surface: Someone peering at a wealthy man's mistress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Peer at' reads as look closely at; Peer is a lord and 'at' merely links.
explanation.definitionFit: A peer is a member of the nobility, a titled nobleman.

clue.text: "Begin cycling!" "I won't!"

indicators.note: cycling means the letters rotate round, the last moving to the front

blocks.note: to open is to begin

explanation.surface: An exchange where one person urges another to start pedalling and gets a refusal.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface has a bike ride; 'cycling' rotates the letters of open.
explanation.definitionFit: Nope is a casual form of no, a flat refusal like I won't.

clue.text: Take priest to outwardly conscious survivors

indicators.note: outwardly means only the outside, the first and last letters

blocks.note: R stands for recipe, Latin for take, on prescriptions
Eli is the priest in the Book of Samuel
first and last letters of conscious

explanation.surface: Bringing a priest to someone who is still outwardly conscious.
explanation.definitionFit: Relics are things that have survived from the past, so they are survivors.

clue.text: Current number (over 50) conforming with the rules

indicators.note: the number is spread over the other piece, so it wraps around it

blocks.note: I is the symbol for electric current
nine is a number
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A number currently over fifty that complies with regulations.
explanation.walkthrough: L goes after the first letter of the number.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in line with the rules means complying with them, so in line means conforming.

clue.text: Sanctimonious type in pub a Republican, I understand

blocks.note: PH is the map abbreviation for public house
taken as written
R for Republican
taken as written
I see means I understand

explanation.surface: A preachy person in a bar turns out to be a Republican, so I gather.
explanation.definitionFit: The Pharisees are portrayed in the Gospels as self-righteous, so a pharisee is a hypocritically pious person.
